examples.en: My husband and I made our family plan together.
A couple should decide on family planning together.
There used to be many family planning campaigns.

examples.ko: 가족계획 때문에 아이를 늦게 가지기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to have kids later because of our family plans.
I got family planning counseling at the health center.
Our family plans differed, so we talked for a long time.

explain: 아이를 몇 명 낳을지, 언제 낳을지 계획하는 것을 말해요. 1960~80년대 정부 캠페인에서 많이 나온 말이라 지금은 조금 옛날 느낌이 있어요. 요즘 대화에서는 '아이 계획'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It means planning how many children to have and when. The word was heavily used in government campaigns from the 1960s to the 1980s, so it now sounds a little dated. In modern conversation people also say '아이 계획'.

examples.en: He's sly, so it's hard to trust him.
Don't be fooled by deceitful words.
They say people's hearts are fickle indeed.
His attitude turned slippery once he got money.
I dislike the way he smiles so slyly.

examples.ko: 저는 간사하지 않은 사람과 친구가 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to be friends with someone who isn't deceitful.

explain: 자기에게 이득이 되면 태도를 쉽게 바꾸고 아첨하는 사람에게 쓰는 부정적인 말이에요. '마음이 간사하다'는 나도 모르게 편한 쪽으로 바뀐다는 뜻으로 자신에게도 써요.
explain_en: A negative word for someone who changes attitude easily when it benefits them and flatters people. 마음이 간사하다 is also said about oneself, meaning your heart drifts to the easier side.

examples.en: Our team leader is really strict.
The successful applicants were decided after a strict review.

examples.ko: 그 집주인은 계약 조건이 깐깐해서 힘들었어요.
examples.en: That landlord's contract terms were demanding, so it was hard.
He is a person who checks everything, so he makes few mistakes.
My mother is picky when choosing ingredients.
The interviewer's questions were stricter than I expected.

explain: '깐깐하다'는 작은 것까지 꼼꼼히 따지고 쉽게 허락하지 않는 사람이나 일에 써요. '꼼꼼하다'는 칭찬이 많지만 깐깐하다는 상대하기 조금 피곤하다는 느낌이 있어요. 비슷한 '까다롭다'는 취향이 많아서 맞추기 어려운 쪽이에요.
explain_en: 깐깐하다 describes a person or process that checks even small details and does not give permission easily. 꼼꼼하다 is often praise, but 깐깐하다 carries a feeling that the person is a bit tiring to deal with. The similar 까다롭다 leans toward having many preferences that are hard to satisfy.

examples.ko: 어머니는 성실한 사람이 좋은 남편감이라고 하세요.
examples.en: My mother says a diligent person makes good husband material.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 어디 내놔도 훌륭한 남편감이에요.
examples.en: He's excellent husband material anywhere.
They say it's not easy to find good husband material.
My aunt introduced me to a decent prospective husband.

examples.ko: 요리 잘하는 남자가 인기 있는 남편감이래요.
examples.en: They say men who cook well are popular husband material.
My friend wants a kind person as a husband.

explain: '-감'은 어떤 역할에 어울리는 후보를 말해서 '신랑감', '사윗감'처럼 써요. 사람을 조건으로 평가하는 느낌이 있어서 말할 상황을 가려 쓰세요.
explain_en: The suffix '-감' means a candidate suited for a role, as in '신랑감' and '사윗감'. It can sound like judging a person by conditions, so choose the situation carefully.

examples.en: My younger sibling is a well-known bookworm.
The teacher's room is full of books because they love reading.

examples.ko: 저도 독서광이 되고 싶은데 시간이 없어요.
examples.en: I want to be a bookworm too, but I have no time.
Being a bookworm, I don't put my book down even on the subway.
I heard that author was a bookworm from a young age.
I joined an online group where bookworms gather.

explain: 책을 아주 많이 읽는 사람이에요. '책벌레'도 비슷한 말인데, 더 친근하고 가볍게 들려요. '-광'은 '영화광, 축구광'처럼 어떤 것에 푹 빠진 사람을 말해요.
explain_en: It means a person who reads a great many books. '책벌레' is similar but sounds friendlier and lighter. The suffix '-광' marks someone absorbed in something, as in '영화광' and '축구광'.

examples.ko: 우리 형은 말수가 적지만 정말 듬직해요.
examples.en: My older brother doesn't talk much, but he's really dependable.

examples.ko: 듬직한 아들이 곁에 있어서 아버지는 든든하세요.
examples.en: With a dependable son beside him, his father feels secure.

examples.ko: 체격도 크고 성격도 듬직해서 믿음이 가요.
examples.en: He's big and steady in character, so I trust him.
That player looks solid and reliable even though he's young.

examples.ko: 듬직하게 곁을 지켜 주는 친구가 있어서 마음이 편해요.
examples.en: I feel at ease because I have a friend who steadily stays by my side.

examples.ko: 못 본 사이에 동생이 어느새 듬직해졌어요.
examples.en: While I wasn't looking, my younger brother has become dependable.

explain: '믿음직하다'와 비슷하지만, 몸집이나 태도가 묵직하고 의젓해서 믿음이 갈 때 더 잘 어울려요. 보통 사람에게 쓰고, 칭찬하는 말이에요. '든든하다'는 의지가 되어 마음이 놓이는 내 기분을 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It is close to '믿음직하다' (trustworthy), but fits best when someone's build or manner is steady and dignified enough to inspire trust. It is usually used for people and is a compliment. '든든하다' describes the feeling of being reassured by having someone to rely on.

examples.ko: 저는 만화 마니아라서 신간이 나오면 바로 사요.
examples.en: I'm a comic book enthusiast, so I buy new volumes right away.
That shop is famous among coffee enthusiasts.

examples.ko: 마니아층이 두터운 영화라서 팬 모임도 있어요.
examples.en: The film has a devoted following, so there is even a fan club.
My father is a camping enthusiast.
It's a hidden restaurant that only enthusiasts know about.
I started as an enthusiast, but now I'm an expert.

explain: '팬'은 사람(가수, 배우)을 좋아하고, 마니아는 물건, 취미, 분야를 깊이 좋아해요. '커피 마니아'처럼 앞에 대상을 붙여요. 영어 'maniac'은 부정적일 수 있지만 한국어 마니아는 대체로 좋은 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: A 팬 likes a person such as a singer or actor, while a 마니아 deeply likes things, hobbies, or fields. Put the object in front, as in 커피 마니아. The English word 'maniac' can be negative, but Korean 마니아 is mostly used in a good sense.

examples.en: People called him a dreamer.
I'm closer to a dreamer than a realist.

examples.ko: 이 소설의 주인공은 꿈 많은 몽상가예요.
examples.en: The main character of this novel is a dreamer full of dreams.
Dreamers sometimes change the world.

examples.ko: 몽상가인 동생은 매일 새 계획을 세워요.
examples.en: My younger brother, a dreamer, makes new plans every day.

examples.ko: 몽상가처럼 살지 말고 한 걸음씩 가 보세요.
examples.en: Don't live like a dreamer; go step by step.

explain: 현실과 먼 꿈을 꾸는 사람을 말해요. 놀리거나 비판하는 말로 쓰일 때도 있고, 새로운 것을 꿈꾸는 사람을 멋있게 말할 때도 있어요. 반대로는 '현실주의자'라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a person who dreams of things far from reality. It can be a mild criticism or teasing, but it can also be admiring toward someone who dreams of new things. The opposite is '현실주의자' (realist).

examples.en: I'm really happy to have met my lifelong partner.
He calls his wife the companion of his life.

examples.ko: 좋은 반려자는 힘들 때 곁에 있어 줘요.
examples.en: A good partner stays by your side when times are hard.

examples.ko: 반려자와 함께 늙어 가는 것이 꿈이에요.
examples.en: My dream is to grow old together with my partner.

examples.ko: 결혼식에서 서로에게 평생 반려자가 되겠다고 약속했어요.
examples.en: At the wedding, they promised to be each other's lifelong partners.

examples.ko: 여행에서는 마음 맞는 반려자가 있으면 좋아요.
examples.en: On a trip, it's nice to have a like-minded companion.

explain: 주로 배우자를 따뜻하게 부를 때 쓰는 말로, '인생의 반려자'라는 짝이 가장 흔해요. 일상 대화에서는 '남편/아내'라고 하고, 축사나 편지, 글에서 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is mainly a warm way to refer to a spouse, and '인생의 반려자' (life partner) is the most common pairing. In daily talk people say '남편' or '아내', while this appears more in congratulatory speeches, letters and writing.

examples.en: My younger sibling has a lively personality.
She greeted me in a bright voice.

examples.ko: 그 옷을 입으니까 더 발랄해 보여요.
examples.en: You look more perky in that outfit.
The new employee laughed brightly.
The kid who used to be bubbly is quiet lately.
This song is upbeat, so it lifts my mood.

explain: 주로 젊은 사람의 밝고 생기 있는 분위기에 써요. 어른이나 나이 많은 분에게는 잘 안 써요. '명랑하다'는 성격이 밝다는 뜻이고, '발랄하다'는 통통 튀는 느낌이 더 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a bright, lively air, mostly for young people, and is rarely used for older adults. 명랑하다 means a cheerful personality, while 발랄하다 adds a bouncy, springy feel.

examples.en: That judge is famous for fair rulings.
To become a judge, you have to study for a long time.
The courtroom went quiet at the judge's single remark.
Young judges have started their new jobs.
My older sister has dreamed of being a judge since childhood.
What a judge needs is fairness.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '판사'를 더 많이 쓰고, '법관'은 뉴스나 글에서 판사를 넓게 가리킬 때 나와요. 그래서 '법관'은 조금 딱딱한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: In everyday talk people say 판사 more often. 법관 appears in news and writing as a broader, more formal word for judges, so it sounds stiff.

examples.en: The weather today is really changeable.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 마음이 변덕맞아서 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: That friend is so fickle that it's hard to trust them.

examples.ko: 변덕맞은 손님 때문에 주문을 세 번이나 바꿨어요.
examples.en: Because of a fickle customer, we changed the order three times.
Why do you change your words so fickly?
Please don't tease me by saying I'm too fickle.
My younger sibling's mood is often changeable.

explain: '변덕스럽다'가 더 무난하고, '변덕맞다'는 조금 더 거칠고 입말 느낌이에요. 사람에게 직접 말하면 비난처럼 들려요. 날씨나 기분이 자주 바뀔 때도 써요.
explain_en: '변덕스럽다' is the more neutral word, while '변덕맞다' sounds a bit rougher and more colloquial. Said to a person directly, it sounds like criticism. It can also describe weather or moods that change often.

examples.en: He was called a turncoat by his colleagues.
It's not easy to forgive a turncoat.
We learned a story about a turncoat in history class.
In the movie, the turncoat regrets it at the end.
Nobody believed the turncoat's words.
The word 'turncoat' is a very heavy expression.

explain: 원래 편을 배신하고 돌아선 사람을 강하게 비난하는 말이에요. 일상에서 친구를 가볍게 '배신자'라고 놀리는 것과 달리, 정치나 역사 이야기에서 무겁게 쓰여요.
explain_en: This is a strong word of condemnation for someone who betrayed their side and turned away. Unlike lightly teasing a friend as a '배신자' (traitor) in daily life, it is used heavily in politics and history.

examples.en: Our youngest is the family's bundle of good luck.

examples.ko: 아기가 태어난 뒤로 일이 잘 풀려서 복덩어리라고 불러요.
examples.en: Things went well after the baby was born, so we call him our lucky charm.

examples.ko: 이 강아지는 우리 집에 온 복덩어리가 틀림없어요.
examples.en: This puppy must be a blessing that came to our home.
The new employee seems like a real stroke of luck.
I'm happy that such a blessing of a daughter-in-law joined the family.
I came home from the hospital holding our little bundle of luck.

explain: 집이나 모임에 들어와 좋은 일을 가져다주는 사람에게 애정을 담아 쓰는 말이에요. 아기, 새 식구, 새 직원에게 자주 써요. 비슷한 말로 '복덩이'도 있어요.
explain_en: It is an affectionate word for someone who brings good fortune to a home or group. It is often used for babies, new family members and new coworkers. '복덩이' is a similar word.

examples.ko: 그 애는 새침데기라서 처음엔 말을 잘 안 해요.
examples.en: She's a bit aloof, so she doesn't talk much at first.

examples.ko: 새침데기처럼 굴더니 알고 보니 아주 다정해요.
examples.en: He acted all stuck-up, but it turns out he's very kind.

examples.ko: 우리 반 새침데기가 오늘 웃는 걸 처음 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw our class's aloof girl smile for the first time today.

examples.ko: 내 동생은 새침데기지만 친구들에게 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: My younger sister is a bit prim, but she's popular with her friends.
The aloof cat doesn't like being petted.
People mistake her for a snob.

explain: 쌀쌀맞게 보이거나 도도한 척하는 사람을 조금 놀리듯 부르는 말이에요. 주로 여자아이나 여자에게 많이 쓰고, 친한 사이에서는 귀엽게 말할 수 있지만 모르는 사람에게는 실례가 될 수 있어요. '깍쟁이'와 비슷하지만 '깍쟁이'에는 인색하다는 뜻도 있어요.
explain_en: It teasingly names someone who seems cool and standoffish. It is used mostly for girls and women; among close people it can sound cute, but to strangers it can be rude. It is similar to '깍쟁이', but '깍쟁이' can also mean stingy.

en: trust; have confidence in; entrust with work

examples.en: The boss trusts that employee a lot.
A teacher whom everyone trusts has newly arrived.

examples.ko: 팀장님이 저를 신임해서 큰 일을 맡겼어요.
examples.en: My team leader trusted me and gave me a big job.

examples.ko: 국민이 신임한 대통령이라도 실수를 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even a president the people trusted can make mistakes.

examples.ko: 저를 신임하지 않으면 이 일은 못 해요.
examples.en: If you do not trust me, I cannot do this job.

examples.ko: 앞으로도 신임할 수 있는 사람이 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to be someone people can trust from now on.

explain: '신임하다'는 사람의 능력을 믿고 일을 맡긴다는 느낌이라서 직장이나 조직 이야기에 많이 나와요. 친구를 믿을 때는 '믿다'를 쓰고, 마음을 놓는 느낌일 때는 '신뢰하다'가 더 가까워요. '신임을 얻다', '신임을 받다'처럼 명사 '신임'과도 자주 써요.
explain_en: 신임하다 has the feeling of trusting someone's ability enough to give them work, so it shows up in workplace and organization talk. For a friend you use 믿다, and 신뢰하다 is closer to relying with peace of mind. The noun also appears as 신임을 얻다 or 신임을 받다.

examples.ko: 교실 뒤에서 친구들이 쑥덕쑥덕 이야기하고 있어요.
examples.en: My friends are whispering at the back of the classroom.

examples.ko: 제가 들어가자 사람들이 쑥덕쑥덕 말하다가 갑자기 조용해졌어요.
examples.en: When I walked in, people were whispering and then suddenly went quiet.
The neighborhood ladies are whispering rumors to each other.
What are you two whispering about so secretly?

examples.ko: 회의 중에 뒤에서 쑥덕쑥덕하는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear whispering from behind during the meeting.

examples.ko: 아이들이 선물을 숨기고 쑥덕쑥덕 작전을 짜요.
examples.en: The kids hide the present and whisper as they plan their scheme.

explain: 남이 들으면 안 되는 이야기나 소문, 흉을 작은 소리로 주고받는 느낌이 있어요. '속닥속닥', '수군수군'과 비슷하게 쓰는데, 뒷말하는 분위기일 때 특히 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It carries the feel of exchanging quiet talk, rumors or gossip that others shouldn't hear. It is close to '속닥속닥' and '수군수군', and fits especially well when the mood is one of talking behind someone's back.

examples.en: I'm still a greenhorn, so I lack experience.
The seniors still treat me like a kid.
I heard that rookie already won the competition.

examples.ko: 애송이 시절에는 실수도 정말 많이 했어요.
examples.en: In my greenhorn days, I made so many mistakes.
Don't act like a kid; take some responsibility.
They looked down on him as a rookie and ended up losing the match.

explain: 나이가 어리거나 경험이 적은 사람을 약간 낮추어 부르는 말이에요. '풋내기'와 비슷하고, 윗사람이 아랫사람에게 쓰거나 자기 자신을 낮출 때 써요. 처음 본 사람에게 쓰면 기분 나쁘게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a slightly belittling word for someone young or inexperienced. It is similar to '풋내기', and is used by a senior toward a junior, or when people put themselves down. Using it on someone you've just met can sound insulting.

examples.en: He is a famous linguist who studies Korean.

examples.ko: 언어학자가 되려면 대학에서 언어학을 공부해야 해요.
examples.en: To become a linguist, you have to study linguistics at university.
The class taught by the professor, who is a linguist, is the most fun.
Linguists observe how language changes.
I've dreamed of becoming a linguist since I was little.

examples.ko: 언어학자의 설명을 들으니 문법이 쉽게 이해됐어요.
examples.en: After hearing the linguist's explanation, I understood the grammar easily.

explain: 외국어를 잘하는 사람이나 통역사와는 달라요. 언어 자체의 구조나 변화를 연구하는 사람을 말해요. 그래서 여러 언어를 못해도 언어학자가 될 수 있어요.
explain_en: This is different from someone who is good at foreign languages or an interpreter. A linguist studies the structure and change of language itself, so a person can be a linguist without speaking many languages.

examples.en: That person is no pushover.

examples.ko: 새로 온 팀장님이 여간내기가 아니라서 긴장돼요.
examples.en: The new team leader is formidable, so I'm nervous.

examples.ko: 저 가게 사장님은 여간내기가 아닌 것 같아요.
examples.en: That shop owner seems like no ordinary person.

examples.ko: 동생이 여간내기가 아니라서 아무도 못 속여요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is so sharp that nobody can fool them.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 여간내기는 아니니까 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: That player is no easy opponent, so we have to be careful.
I heard that she's quite a formidable person.

explain: 거의 '여간내기가 아니다'처럼 부정과 함께 써서, 만만치 않고 보통 사람과 다르다는 말이 돼요. 능력이 뛰어나서 감탄할 때도, 상대하기 까다로워서 경계할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: The new teacher is no pushover.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보통 사람이 아니다'라는 말을 그대로 풀면 되지만, 실제로는 능력이 대단하거나 만만치 않다는 감탄·경계를 담은 굳은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It literally says 'not an ordinary person', but in practice it is a set phrase carrying admiration or wariness about someone formidable.

explain_en: It is almost always used with a negative, as in '여간내기가 아니다', meaning someone is not to be underestimated. It can express admiration for someone's ability or wariness about someone hard to deal with.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 나이는 어려도 정말 영악해요.
examples.en: That child is really shrewd even though he's young.
Be careful not to be fooled by a crafty merchant.

examples.ko: 동생이 영악하게 부모님께 용돈을 받아 냈어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling cleverly got pocket money out of our parents.
That friend is shrewd, but has a warm heart.

examples.ko: 영악해서 손해 보는 일은 절대 안 해요.
examples.en: He's so shrewd that he never does anything that costs him.

examples.ko: 영악했던 그 후배는 결국 먼저 승진했어요.
examples.en: That shrewd junior colleague ended up getting promoted first.

explain: 똑똑하다는 뜻이지만 '영악하다'는 자기에게 이익이 되게 꾀를 잘 쓴다는 느낌이 있어서 칭찬만으로 들리지 않을 때가 많아요. 순수하게 머리가 좋다고 칭찬할 때는 '영특하다'나 '똑똑하다'가 더 알맞아요.
explain_en: It means smart, but '영악하다' suggests using tricks to benefit oneself, so it often doesn't sound like pure praise. To simply praise someone's brains, '영특하다' or '똑똑하다' fits better.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 천생 예술가라서 늘 그림을 그려요.
examples.en: My friend is a born artist, so he's always drawing.

examples.ko: 선생님은 천생 교사라서 쉬는 날에도 학생 걱정을 하세요.
examples.en: Our teacher is a natural-born teacher and worries about students even on days off.

examples.ko: 그 사람, 천생 어린아이 같아서 미워할 수가 없어요.
examples.en: He's just like a child by nature, so I can't hate him.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 취향이 똑같아서 천생연분이라고 해요.
examples.en: The two have identical tastes, so people call them a perfect match.

examples.ko: 싸운 적도 없이 십 년을 산다니 천생연분이 따로 없네요.
examples.en: Ten years together without a single fight? They're truly meant for each other.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 천생 농사꾼이라 은퇴하고도 밭에 나가세요.
examples.en: Grandpa is a born farmer, so he still goes to the field after retiring.

explain: '천생 ○○이다'처럼 뒤에 직업이나 성격을 나타내는 명사가 와서, 그 모습이 몸에 밴 듯 타고났다는 느낌을 줘요. 칭찬일 때도, 어쩔 수 없다는 뉘앙스일 때도 있어요. '천생연분'은 이 말이 들어간 굳은 표현으로 부부나 연인에게 많이 써요.

phrases.en: That couple is a perfect match.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하늘이 맺어 준 것처럼 잘 맞는 인연을 말해요. 부부나 연인에게 쓰는 좋은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means a pairing so fitting it seems arranged by heaven. It is a warm compliment for couples.

explain_en: It is followed by a noun for a job or personality, as in '천생 ○○이다', giving the feel that someone is that way by nature. It can be praise or a shrug that it can't be helped. '천생연분' is a fixed expression built on it, often used for couples.

examples.en: My older sister is a cellist who works in an orchestra.
I cried after hearing the cellist play.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 첼리스트가 되는 게 꿈이었어요.
examples.en: Since I was little, my dream was to become a cellist.

examples.ko: 그 첼리스트는 공연 때마다 같은 곡을 연주해요.
examples.en: That cellist plays the same piece at every concert.
I want to learn the cello from a cellist.
The cellists came on stage and took their seats.

explain: 악기 이름 뒤에 '-리스트/-니스트'가 붙은 직업 이름이에요. '바이올리니스트', '피아니스트'처럼 말해요. 악기는 '첼로'이고 '첼로 연주자'라고 풀어서 말할 수도 있어요.
explain_en: This is a job name formed by adding a '-리스트/-니스트' ending to an instrument, like '바이올리니스트' and '피아니스트'. The instrument is '첼로', and you can also say '첼로 연주자' (cello player).

examples.en: Our dog is really loyal.
That retainer was a loyal man to the king.

examples.ko: 충성스러운 친구가 한 명만 있어도 든든해요.
examples.en: Even one loyal friend is reassuring.
He worked devotedly and was recognized by the boss.
The loyal subordinate stayed to the very end.

examples.ko: 이 경찰견은 충성스러워서 주인을 잘 따라요.
examples.en: This police dog is loyal, so it follows its owner well.

explain: 윗사람, 나라, 주인에게 마음을 다하는 모습에 써요. 개 같은 동물에게 칭찬으로도 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 윗사람을 잘 따른다는 느낌이 강해요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '충성스러워요', '충성스러운'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: Use it for wholehearted devotion to a superior, a country, or an owner. It is also used as praise for animals such as dogs. Said about a person, it carries a strong sense of following a superior well. It is a ㅂ-irregular word, so it becomes '충성스러워요' and '충성스러운'.

en: discipline; admonish; caution; teach a lesson

examples.en: The teacher quietly admonished the student who was late.

examples.ko: 부모님은 아이를 너무 심하게 훈계하지 않아요.
examples.en: My parents don't lecture the child too harshly.

examples.ko: 사람들 앞에서 후배를 훈계하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't lecture a junior in front of other people.
Grandfather always lectures us to be polite.
Even when I lecture him, the child only pretends to listen.

examples.ko: 그는 친구를 훈계할 만큼 잘난 사람이 아니에요.
examples.en: He is not a person who is good enough to lecture his friends.

explain: 윗사람이 아랫사람에게 잘못을 고치라고 타이를 때 쓰는 말이라, 친구 사이에는 어색해요. 친구에게는 '충고하다'가 자연스럽고, '타이르다'는 더 부드러운 느낌이에요. 훈계 내용이 맞더라도 말투가 길어지면 '잔소리'로 들려요.
explain_en: This is for a senior person telling a junior to correct a mistake, so it sounds awkward between friends. With friends, '충고하다' is more natural, and '타이르다' feels gentler. Even when the content is right, a long lecturing tone gets heard as '잔소리' (nagging).
